reel.caption:
Missed a few EMIs: can the lender take your car by force?

In September 2026 the Supreme Court ordered ₹10 lakh compensation for a borrower whose financed truck was seized and sold without due process, and told the RBI to make lenders follow its recovery rules.
Lenders and recovery agents can't use force, threats or stealth, even after a default. You should get a notice before repossession and a chance to pay before the vehicle is sold.
If it goes wrong, complain in writing to the lender first, then to the RBI ombudsman.
Missing EMIs still has real costs: penalties, a lower credit score, and legal repossession.

Did you know recovery agents have rules to follow?

Sources: two personal-finance news reports on the September 2026 Supreme Court judgment (17 and 23 Sep 2026).

For education only. Not investment advice.
